events.note: Zone briefings and how your companions react to each outcome.

items.d: The ground is overgrown with weeds, which provide soil retention and shelter for small animals. Growing grass and bushes from barren sand is the first step in terraforming in the barrenlands.

items.tag:
Grants more **Training Handbooks** when deployed. Every <Flower Bush> causes all Operators to recover **1** HP per second.

Transform: When there are **5** <Bushes> on the field at the same time, all deployed <Bushes> and future deployed <Bushes> become <Flower Bushes>.
items.d: Bushes with flowers growing from them. The stabilized soil and water environment has attracted more creatures, and with them the seeds of flowering plants. The flower bushes are becoming increasingly biodiverse, and plants with medicinal value can be harvested from them.

items.tag: All Operators gain Max HP **+25**, plus **+5** Max HP for every <Rock> in the **8** surrounding tiles.
items.d: Rocks formed from complex sediments. They contain various minerals and are important in construction and industry. Mining rocks and extracting metals from them is a necessary step for building an industry in the barrenlands.

items.tag:
All Operators gain Max HP **+500**.
Transform: <Rocks> deployed in a **3×3** formation become a <Mountain>.
items.d: Rugged mountains that are home to a variety of climates and ecosystems. Home to many plants and animals, as well as rich metal deposits.

Many types of trees grow from the soil, providing shade with their sparse canopy. Trees in the barrenlands take root deeply, helping to stabilize the loose, sandy soil. The decay of fallen leaves helps nurture even more life.

items.tag:
All Operators gain ATK **+20**.

Transform: <Woods> deployed in a **1×3** formation become a <Forest>.
items.d: A thick, lush forest. As trees compete for sunlight, they create more room for those who live beneath their canopies. Fungi grow on fallen trunks, while those who feed upon the fungi are fed upon by larger creatures, which in turn nourish new saplings with their carcasses.

items.tag:
Can only be deployed on map edge or in the **4** adjacent tiles of a <River>. Increases nearby <Terrain> effects. Irrigates any ground tiles in the **4** adjacent tiles, turning them into <Loam>.
<Loam>: Operators on it gain **+50%** ATK and HP; <Farmland>/<Greenhouse Shed> production is increased.
items.d: Man-made river channel, drawing water from nearby. A river quenches the barrenlands, supplies water to agricultural and industrial facilities, and maintains the fragile stability of frontier outposts.

items.tag:
Operators in the **4** adjacent tiles **take damage** each second and have **+50%** ATK.

Transform: When there are <Originium Formations> around a <River>, any connected <River>/<Loam> become <Polluted River>/<Polluted Loam>.
items.d: River polluted by active Originium. Crystal-littered banks are a frequent sight in Catastrophe-heavy areas, turning the river into a different color.

items.tag:
When skill is activated, if there are other <Loaders> connected by <Rivers>, creates a transport boat that travels along the <River> to the corresponding <Loader>, providing resources when it arrives. The further the destination, the more resources it grants on arrival.

 Transform: <Rivers> become <Loaders> if there is a <Sensor Hub> in the **4** adjacent tiles. (Each <Sensor Hub> can only create one <Loader>)
items.d: Light loader designed for canals. A smart sensor system helps distribute supplies to Rhodes Island cargo boats. The more difficult the environment, the more important teamwork is in order to overcome the challenges.

items.tag: Deploy a <Surveyor> to turn it into an <Originium Mine>.

Grants a small amount of **Packaged Cores** when defeated.

Transform: Deploy a <Surveyor> on a <Rich Vein> to turn it into an <Originium Mine>.
items.d: An Originium vein that has been fully surveyed. Rhodes Island is moving forward with the mining operation after a careful review. Originium ore is the foundation of industry, but the extraction and refining process is a major source of pollution.

items.tag:
Grants a small amount of **Packaged Cores** when defeated.

Transform: <Formation Stabilizer> skill destroys itself and all <Originium Formations> within Attack Range, turning its own tile into an <Originium Mine>.
items.d: An Originium vein that has been fully surveyed. Rhodes Island is moving forward with the mining operation after a careful review. Originium ore is the foundation of industry, but the extraction and refining process is a major source of pollution.

items.tag: Can attack after deployment while skill is active, dealing Arts damage. If deployed on a <Rich Vein>, turns it into an <Originium Mine> after skill ends.
items.d: Portable surveying equipment for field survey missions. The interface is sleek and simple to use, but operators are required to adhere to the manual's instructions to avoid accidentally triggering its fire control system.

Unstable Originium formations that continue to expand. Wind and water can carry active Originium particles a great distance. If left unchecked, they could lead to immeasurable consequences, even Catastrophes.

items.tag:
Must be deployed on an <Originium Formation>. Gains **1** SP per second for each <Originium Formation> within Attack Range;
when skill is activated, destroys self and any <Originium Formations> within Attack Range, turning its own tile into an <Originium Mine>.
items.d: Emergency pollution cleanup equipment powered directly by airborne active Originium particles. Effective at reducing the risk of Originium explosions in an area, but ultimately the pollution problem must be tackled at the source.

items.tag: Gains SP when Infected Creatures are defeated; if said Creatures are defeated within its Attack Range, gains doubled SP.
items.d: A catalytic reactor that effectively collects active Originium particles, generating clean energy for the frontier outpost.

items.tag:
Gains SP when Infected Creatures are defeated; if said Creatures are defeated within its Attack Range, gains doubled SP.

Transform: <Originium Recycler> becomes <Polluted Recycler> when there is an <Originium Formation> around it.
items.d: When captured active Originium particles exceed a certain threshold, the Originium Recycler begins to operate differently, concentrating active Originium particles to generate Originium fuel that is used in the outpost's factories.

items.tag:
Gains SP whenever a new Armory Plug-in is obtained; when skill is activated, grants **1Improved Armory Plug-in** or **Advanced Armory Plug-in**; for every **2** skill activations, grant **1** more <Plug-in Upgrade Depot>.
<Plug-in Upgrade Depot> spawns 1 **Teary Detective** or **Defense Crusher** when skill is activated. Defeat them to upgrade 1 random equipped Armory Plug-in.
items.d: Mobile industrial platform equipped with a foundry module, traveling across rough terrain to where the raw materials are produced, processing them directly at the source and reducing time overhead.

items.tag: Recovers SP over time. **Loses SP** when an enemy passes through.
items.d: Fenced-off land that can be used to grow crops. The soil nutrient mix can be adjusted based on the crop, and small cultivators are available to prevent soil crusting.

items.tag:
Recovers SP over time. **Loses SP** when an enemy passes through.

 Transform: <Farmland> deployed in a **1×3** formation becomes a <Greenhouse Shed>.
items.d: Greenhouse shed for scaled agricultural production, increasing efficiency while reducing the impact that natural conditions have on agriculture. The lighting, temperature, and humidity can be adjusted in zones based on plant needs.

items.tag: Every 5s, restores the SP of Production Modules within Attack Range, and causes all Operator skills to activate automatically (effect does not stack).
items.d: Energy transmission is always a major challenge when building in the barrenlands. A comprehensive and efficient power grid relies on power supply stations like these to act as both hub and node. Rhodes Island's remote computing and deployment strategy has significantly reduced energy loss.

items.tag: Recovers SP when Production Modules are obtained.
items.d: Libraries continue to play an irreplaceable role in the retention and transmission of knowledge. Although Rhodes Island is equipped with a highly digitized information storage system, tried-and-true pen and paper remain an important medium for passing down skills and experiences.

items.tag: Recovers SP over time; when skill is activated, teleports **1** enemy from this tile to the nearest reachable Operator.
items.d: Sarkaz witchcraft being used to transfer personnel and supplies over vast distances on the battlefield has left a deep impression on observers from many factions. Rhodes Island engineers have made improvements on the ancient witchcraft altar with modern Originium technology.

items.tag:
Recovers SP when Production Modules are obtained; when skill is activated, chance to drop a **Production Module**.

Transform: <Archives> become <Great Libraries> when there is an <Improved Witchcraft Altar> in the **4** adjacent tiles.
items.d: Libraries continue to play an irreplaceable role in the retention and transmission of knowledge. The walls of the library do not represent the boundaries of knowledge, though the size of the shelves have a certain correlation with the depth of acquisition.

items.tag: When skill is activated, spawns an <Advance Detector> in the **4** adjacent tiles. One random enemy within skill range gains **+50%** ATK and Max HP; defeat it to gain **1Basic Armory Plug-in**. The 4th <Advance Detector> spawned this way will not spawn any additional <Advance Detectors> when its skill is activated.
items.d: Detector that Closure designed for the barrenlands. An encrypted ZOOT channel enables remote proxy operation, while environmental data collected by the detectors is analyzed by ZOOT to compute the optimal strategy.

items.tag:
Gains SP every **5**s for each <Advance Detector> and other <Sensor Hub> on the field. Grants **1Plug-in Supply Depot** whenever a **Sponsor Drone** spawned by the skill is defeated.
<Plug-in Supply Depot> Grants 1**Advanced Armory Plug-in** when an enemy spawned by the skill is defeated.

Transform: <Advance Sensors> deployed in a **3×3** formation become a <Sensor Hub>.
items.d: Sensor hub that Closure designed for the barrenlands, comprising multiple Advance Detectors. The computing cluster allows ZOOT to establish more automated patrol and detection programs to ensure the safety of the outpost.

items.tag: Recovers SP when an enemy is defeated in the 8 surrounding tiles; chance to grant **1Basic Armory Plug-in** when skill is activated.
items.d: The scars of the Battle of Londinium continue to haunt Victoria. Those who clean up the battlefield have no way of knowing whether they are digging up something useful, or waking a blood artifact from its slumber.

items.tag:

Vannini was still a child at the time, and she hadn't been at the workshop for very long. The Notarial Hall sent over her mother's patron firearm. She held onto that filthy gun, still covered in bloodstains... You didn't want to think too hard about where they came from.
So you brought her to the workroom, explaining to her how to clean a gun. You asked her if she needed help, but she said nothing. You wanted to stay and keep her company, but then you saw her lower her head.
You were at a loss, thinking she wanted to be by herself for a while. With a sigh, you turned and headed back upstairs. The moment you heard glass shattering, you hurried back downstairs. The workbench was completely covered in solvent, and all Vannini did was tremble as she stood in shock at the scene of the 'accident'.
You wanted to say something to console her, but it was clear that no matter what you said, she'd only reply with silence. She had lost her family and was suffering. You knew this much, and tried many times to find an inroad to her heart, but you never found the right place to start.

You relive the fatigue you felt at the time, ignoring the fact that the bottle had shattered long ago.

In the evening, you receive a greeting from an old friend. As you think back to the little moments when you were friends, your mind is left in disarray.

The silver papal gun-knight medal, established by then-Pope Ludovico IV on February the 14th of 1029, was made to honor trainee knights who displayed especially outstanding skill, allowing them to skip the final examinations and formally join the gun-knights early. The youngest of these recipients, Patrizion, was only twenty-six years of age.

At the award ceremony, you were part of the crowd. You saw the pope himself pin the medal onto Patrizion. Your younger cousin Gia was holding your hand tightly, transmitting both her excitement and nervousness to you.
After paying his respects to the pope, he scanned the crowd anxiously. You and Gia held your arms up high, shouting as much as you could. The moment he saw the two of you, he broke out into a smile.
You looked at him as he looked back, your heart full of pride. The two of you had a pact. If he managed to get this medal, then you'd entrust that giant gun you made recently to him. You had voiced your doubts, but in your heart, you knew there was nobody else worthy to wield your 'masterpiece' aside from that smiling, splendid little bastard.

You don't answer his message, throwing your communicator aside in irritation, completely forgetting that, at the time, it wasn't you who locked eyes with him, but Gia.

In the depths of the fridge there is always a carton of your sinful pleasure hidden away: ice cream. In the early morning, you dig out a big scoop, but just as you are about to bring it to your beak, there is a knock at the door.

You open the door to see Idida, the neighbors' young daughter, holding a thick stack of leaflets.
With a resigned sigh, you say: 'You know it's not even five in the morning yet, right, kid?'
The girl simply bats her eyelashes before letting out a sly smile: 'But you're a nocturnal Liberi, right?' You sigh and take a leaflet, the giant cautionary slogan domineering your view and reminding you to avoid harmful sugar.
You are reminded of the pamphlets stuffing your mailbox, inviting you to take part in neighborhood meetings every week, where discussions on how to expel dessert shops from the neighborhood—no, all of Laterano—take place. You suddenly realize why this house was so cheap. No ordinary Lateran could tolerate living next to these insane dentists who wouldn't stop talking about fluoridated toothpaste.
'Want something to eat before you go, Idida?'
'Thanks, but that's not going to work on me! I won't be tempted by the evil desserts in your fridge!'
'That's not it, Idida. I just thought you still don't fully understand your enemy.'
You wink as you stuff a carton of ice cream into her hands.

In the middle of the night, you knock a few books off the bookshelf. They open as you pick them up, and a report greets you from among the pages. You are reminded of the day you brought Vannini to doctors all across the city.

[Medical Report]
Pagus Faber Central Hospital, Halo Surgery
Patient suffers from a speech impediment, speaking with only great difficulty and with severe lexical deficiency. Patient also shows mild difficulties in reading and writing. Diagnosis is psychogenic aphasia.
Aside from medication, considering the family's particular circumstances, weekly empathy contact sessions at this hospital have been suggested.

You couldn't rely on empathy to read the girl's mind, so at the doctor's suggestion, you bought Little Halo, Little Heart, a series of books about Sankta child psychology. You memorized every passage in those books, but when you saw her stuttering in front of you, the grim reality set in. Every sentence of these lousy books was based on a central premise: both you and your child have big, bright halos on your heads.
But you don't have one—not then, not now. What a shame. Those books were useless to you.

You relive the anxiety and anger you felt at the time, ignoring the fact that you tore these books to shreds in a fit of rage long ago.

At night, you find a piece of cake in the refrigerator. After sating your hunger, you think back to how astonished you were the first time you had it.

Every time they were done with a mission, that one squad would always come to your workshop for weapon maintenance, bringing with them some of that cake you adored.
The Sanktas treated their patron firearms like their babies, hoping you would clean them with utmost gentleness. The Liberi, on the other hand, would always ask you questions with a straight face:
'Can you make the grenade launcher fire further?
'Can you improve the rifling?
'Changing out the attachments is a pain in the ass... Anything you can do to fix it?'
At least, until you told her you could, but first, she had to be okay with swapping out a transmitter, since the current one was barely more than a worn-out lump of iron.
As straight-faced as ever, she said:
'Then swap it already.'
You sighed with relief that this wasn't a patron firearm. If it were, its owner would have been going mad with worry over the damage.
She turned back to her friends, one of them sobbing her eyes out over having to change her gun's sights. Soon after, the corners of the Liberi's mouth turned upwards, and she said rather happily:
'Good thing I don't have a guardian gun.'

You are enraptured by the taste, forgetting that these raisin cakes were never actually that tasty, since there were always pranksters embedding odd-tasting candy in them.

...Patri, Avia's leaving you this necklace. If you ever find the right girl one day, give it to her to wear, then bring her to my grave for me to have a look. July would be best. The jasmines will be in bloom.

That day, you saw Patrizion putting that necklace around Gia's neck as she looked down bashfully.
Their wedding was to be in July, and you were their best man, organizing the entire wedding in the lovebirds' place. When the two of them confessed their relationship to you, at first you were angry at them for hiding it from you, but that anger quickly turned to joy. You had long hoped he would become a part of your family. After all, ever since his grandmother passed, he was the only one left in his.

The necklace comes with news of Gia's death. You endure the grief, forgetting how on that day, you weren't actually that happy. Gia had whispered to you about how her knee was always aching lately.

It's now midnight, and you're still enjoying your sinful ice cream without a care in the land. Suddenly, a wave of knocking hammers at your door. You open it.

You see Idida, her face covered in tears. Her mouth opens wide due to her weeping, and you notice that where her two incisors should be, there are only gaps.
'I'm being punished, all because of your wicked ice cream! My teeth fell out!'
You sigh and hand her some tissues as you try to console her.
'No, you're just at that age when you get new teeth, Idida.'
'Teeth falling out is a punishment! The original sin of the Sankta is loving desserts!'
No matter what you say, she does not stop wailing. Her tears do not stop either, as if her eyes were broken faucets. It is not long before the waste basket is full of soggy tissues.
'What's it gonna take for you to stop crying?'
'*sniff* I don't know either... Right now, it's just my teeth falling out, but what if my halo gets cavities next? There's nothing you can do to make me feel better, just give up.'
'I've got a new flavor of ice cream in my fridge.'
'......'
'Want some?'
'...Yeah.'
'If you have some, will you stop crying?'
The girl sobs as she opens the carton of ice cream. In your heart, you smirk. What Sankta could resist the allure of sweet ice cream? No one, that's who.
'All your teeth will fall out eventually, you know.'
'That's not going to work on me. I don't have teeth—I grind up my food with gastroliths.'

Made from: 100% Paganini feathers
Dry clean only
Do not wash at over 30 degrees
Hang-dry
Iron at low temperature
Do not bleach
—Laundry tag

Whenever Vannini felt cold, she would bury herself in your thick feathers, only sticking her face out once she was nearly out of breath.
Every molting season, you would gather a big sack's worth of feathers and pick out the most beautiful and lustrous ones to make a cape. It took you a good few years to do it, since your feathers were always rather dull and drab from a lack of rest. Once she got the cape, Vannini took about half a day to express her gratitude. It was an incredibly long speech, all in all, but you couldn't have asked for better payment.
You held back tears as you gazed at her. You didn't speak, and she didn't either, electing instead to nervously twiddle her thumbs.

Late at night, you raise your head while in the middle of work to check the time. It's nearly midnight. You remember the last time Seniora Fiammetta came to your workshop. It was rather late at night too.

She was in a gloomy mood as she told you the owner of the 'Gun of the Year' was already far from Laterano, and that before she left, all she did was give Fiammetta a pocket watch, telling her to look after it.
She rubbed her forehead as she grumbled:
'They all got over it, but I just can't... I'm always one step behind them, I get it!
'Just like this watch... That woman went and gave me a watch that can't even keep time.'
You handed her a cup of wine, took the pocket watch she handed to you, and got its mechanism working again, its hands leaping back to life. You suddenly realized why Mostima left her pocket watch with her.
'I think...' You chose your words carefully as you tried to console her.
'Look at the watch, Seniora Fiammetta. The second and minute hands are both swift, but while the hour hand may lag behind them, at midnight the three will always reunite, and a new day will dawn.
'These three hands, they come together to form this watch.'
She sighed, broke out into a smile, then left.

You continue on with your work, so busy you forgot that Fiammetta never came by that day.

Late at night, you take out a letter from inside the safe. A letter Gia entrusted you with to give Patrizion. You never did. You think back.

[Mission Notice]
Date of mission: 07/21
Mission objective: Exiling an Oripathy patient from the Holy City
Executor: Patrizion

From June to July, you looked for Patrizion countless times, hoping there could be some room for negotiation. Even if Gia had to stay at a convent outside the Holy City, it would be fine, but he was silent, spitting out only a single sentence after a long while:
'The Law... cannot be violated.'
You gave Gia a hug before sending her off to the waiting convoy outside the Holy City. It was a raging-hot July, but her hands were ice-cold. Patrizion stood by the convoy, carrying his gun, not saying a word. He glanced incessantly at you and Gia, but he never dared to look the two of you in the face.

You put the letter and the necklace back into the safe, deleting Patrizion's number as you do so. Grief made you forget that you never had his number.

Late at night, you open the miniature fridge under your bed, only to discover you've already eaten all your ice cream. All that is left is a lonely salad. You sigh and open it up, but then a familiar chain of knocks rap against your door.

You open the door, but rather than who you expected, it is your neighbor holding a thick stack of leaflets while inviting you to participate in next week's neighborhood meeting.
You take a leaflet, noting that it is no longer about how to stop desserts from entering the neighborhood, but rather a joint discussion on how to help Idida spread the good word of sugar-free ice cream across all of Laterano.
Your neighbor proudly chats with you about the girl in question.
'Say, thanks to my girl inventing sugar-free ice cream, Laterano will finally receive salvation.
To whoever gave her this revelation, may fluoridated toothpaste bless you!'
You give an embarrassed smile, saying you'll definitely attend if you have the time.
After sending off your neighbor, you return to your desk and prepare to eat your dinner, but once more you are rudely interrupted by more knocking on your door.
You open the door to see Idida smiling a gap-toothed smile.
'As the one who gave me the revelation of sugar-free ice cream, would you like to make an investment?'
'Absolutely not, little girl.'
'Then would you like to try some?'
You note that the leafy greens in the carton have no vinaigrette on them.
'...Yeah.'

We climbed the city outskirts and reached the edge of the plate next to the city. Our makeshift equipment allowed us to bring most of our supplies. The area was eerily quiet despite the many wrecked buildings. As we searched, it became clear that residents had left in a hurry. In one apartment, we found broken and stained dolls on the dinner table, evidence of their hasty departure. Something feels off about this place, but we're determined to complete the mission.
We are currently heading towards the city office as planned. Wish us luck.

items.d: You have collected ample intel on Londinium and its surroundings. I can now formulate the final step of this operation.
items.d2:
We have arrived at the city's auxiliary plates following your route. The mobility layer here is neglected, with broken equipment scattered everywhere. Fortunately, the support structures remain stable, so there's no risk of collapse. In the support layer, we found many residents who fled their homes. A stable society has formed here due to the long-term unrest above. Many fear the Sarkaz and are unwilling to return to the residential layer, describing the city as chaotic. Nevertheless, it remains our objective. We provided necessities to this 'city within a city' before moving on. We are currently heading to the city office as planned.
We are currently heading towards the city office as planned. Please keep comms clear.

items.d2:
In the area with the highest active Originium concentrations, we encountered Sarkaz mercenaries who had retreated from the Redmane Mountains and were left to die in the wastes. They refused our medical aid. When a sudden catastrophe struck, we gave them our equipment. Afterward, some mercenaries decided to join us on our journey to the city in exchange for more supplies, despite being labeled 'traitors' by their peers.
We are currently heading towards the city office as planned, and our team is stronger than when we first set out.

items.d: Your team is adequately prepared and can try to charge straight to the final objective point.
items.d2:
On our way to the Londinium outskirts, we encountered three groups of people. The first group comprised refugees who had fled the city long ago but were stranded on the outskirts due to difficult terrain. They seemed mentally well and adequately supplied, playing cards and chatting as we passed. Closer to the city, we met armed Victorian soldiers, their physical and mental strain evident. Lastly, we came across a distraught group of Londinium residents who had just fled the city. They were in a dire state, trembling as they described how the city was littered with Londinier and Sarkaz corpses and how the remaining survivors were on the brink of collapse. We fear the worst for Londinium.
We are currently heading towards the city office as planned. Hopefully, things are slightly better there.

We ultimately decided to follow the Confessarius's tracks and entered the city via a hidden passage, bringing all our supplies into Londinium. The war ravaged city faces multiple crises: its resources depleted, its people weary, and its future uncertain. We distributed our supplies to those in dire need, though many still remain unhelped. We've also received news that other Rhodes Island teams are arriving in Londinium. Hopefully, our efforts will make a difference.
We are currently executing our mission as planned; thank you for your unwavering support and guidance.

items.d:
That which is in full bloom, is enough to halt spring;
it does not seem to come from the earth, but teems from the courtyard walls,
swaying in all its fragrance. Your smile captivates all beings.
The sounds everywhere tempt the people to run.
With your Arts, you can make those frantic footsteps stop.
Your tendrils embrace the scattered verses and trace them into petals.
You teach everyone to embrace them,
and they unite in laughter.

The damaged wooden core has not broken.
They stagger forward with carving knives and hoes.
Vedunien, we will carve your coffin.
We will pull taut the strings of fate.
From you we will carve keys of black gold.
We will carve the melody of your demise—
We will carve you! We will carve you!

The spires fall silent.
The fountains, lifeless, ooze a red mist.
In the park, crowded Doppelhörner falls silent
Yet you turn around, tears about to dry.

Above the sky, an eternal palace
You climb upwards, trembling
Ascending those chaotic, tumultuous steps
Primordial glyphs wrap around the walls
To the stones within the gaps, they bind you tightly
Their lives as long as the night itself
Serenity is like the veins coursing through you
The stairs hang high in the abyss
leading to the spire where the fog dissipates
Harken, for the spire has never divulged what scenery lies at journey's end.

If the footsteps of life will one day
be buried beneath the dust of time...
then we must never, ever
—halt our steps.

The beasts these days are outrageous.
I did some sweeping just yesterday, and there's already leaves everywhere.
Hey kid, just get rid of them for me, alright?

They're making such a ruckus!
These basorobeasts keep knocking on the trees around my house in the middle of the night.
Get rid of them so I can hand in my manuscripts in time!

Ah...I really want to eat it...
That piping-hot, tender and succulent hornbeast steak.
Please, I beg you! Let me have a taste once more!

My balloons were punctured by the Serrant Fowlbeasts again...
I can't let them destroy my dreams of flying to the skies!
You! Surely you know what to do next!

Oh, life has no way of stopping these sturdy muscles from colliding with each other.
I hear the Direswine is the best at this.
Quickly, you must experience its heart-thumping charge in my stead!

As a fan of mine, you must surely be aware of my latest series—
The No Blink Challenge! The challenger is... a Serrant Fowlbeast!
Gaze straight into that dazzling light, and I will be the last one standing!

Hear me out! I was trying on my new clothes over there.
But a Haribeast suddenly appeared and left my clothes in tatters!
You can get rid of those nasty beasts for me, right?

Cautelotaurs are so good at blocking enemy attacks, how exactly do they do it?
If I can learn their tactics, I'll definitely improve at tower defense games.
Study them well, and teach it to me after.

The road ahead is blazing hot, but still you stand firm and ready.
With this courage, you will surely be able to overcome all your enemies.
We await your triumphant return.

Please collect enough Bone Fragments,
for only I understand the meaning of life contained in them.
Of course, I will let you know too.

Please collect enough of Originium Slug Shells,
for only I understand the meaning of life contained in them.
Of course, I will let you know too.

Please collect enough of Sharp Oxmane Fangs,
for only I understand the meaning of life contained in them.
Of course, I will let you know too.

Please collect enough of Thick Direswine Hide,
for only I understand the meaning of life contained in them.
Of course, I will let you know too.

Please collect enough of 'Monster Tears',
for only I understand the meaning of life contained in them.
Of course, I will let you know too.

The highest altitude record I managed to reach after all my hard work...
was so easily smashed by those flying beasts!
They've made a mockery of me! I demand vengeance!

My research is solely on the beasts' weaknesses.
If you give me enough data, I'll cite you as thanks in my paper.
Damn it, I have to graduate before that geologist does!

The tremors in the forest keep interfering with my seismic data monitoring.
I'll never finish my thesis at this rate...
Help me out! I really want to graduate!

The notes dance in a beautiful, omni-directional, and fiery movement.
This melody... is exclusive to the Pyric Originium Slug.
Please allow me another listen.

Hello, this is a commission designated for you.
We hope you can survive a collision while wearing our latest equipment.
Please rest assured, for the equipment is insured.

Look at how high those fowlbeasts can fly...
I'm afraid they'll plummet to the ground, or maybe they're scared of heights.
Not letting them fly anymore would be a kindness.

Hey, you must have heard of me and my famously hard head.
People say the Gravorobeasts have a much thicker skull, but I don't believe it!
Can you figure out a way to let me fight one?

I admit you have some skills.
But to be strong, one must overcome even tougher challenges.
Complete this commission, and you'll have my approval.

The spikes of the Rainer Haribeast are uniquely shaped and extremely lethal.
Figuring out a way to use them in weapon designs will ensure a steady supply of orders.
Get me some, and I'll compensate you fairly.

The combat skills of a hunter are too much for me...
But to become one, I mustn't give up here!
Can you show me again how a real hunter fights?

items.d: The demise of Famiglia Texas was a result of Siracusa's old order, yet even the fall of such a prominent famiglia did not change anything. The status quo did not change, and the famiglie continued to fight amongst each other. The new Siracusa cannot continue down this path.

Was recommended by a friend, and don't regret it at all. After watching too many shows playing up the greatness of the famiglie, a whole lot of people come to see themselves in the great, heroic mafiosi depicted in those operas. And that's a dangerous thing.

Did the playwright know about the gangsters that got ran out of Siracusa? Their ringleader was a red-haired Vulpo, and the protagonist bore too many similarities to him. Impulsive and arrogant, yet not dislikable at all. The other two brothers, one calm, one brash, matched them perfectly as well!

I heard that the directing team recently won an award. I hope the show actually earned it, and isn’t just another mediocre product propped up to fluff Signora Sicilia. It's not fair to hardworking playwrights.
Still boring as hell.
Some of the details are realistic, uncannily so. The playwright must have some strong opinions about Texas to come up with an ending like that.

This is my first time using this new rating system. It was also my first time watching an opera in a theater, which was kind of strange. By the end, I was shouting along with the others. I might have to ask the author myself – what did he choose at the end? To pick up the phone, or to throw away those old rapiers?

It’s the lowest wise guy who hates his famiglia, all while clinging to it, yearning for it, until he finally betrays the brothers who were there for him all the way up the ladder just to save his own skin. It’s what it is.

Never expected this play to be so long. I fell asleep halfway through, and got woken up by the people next to me. Almost got kicked out of the theater again. Seeing them trying to fluff up the famiglie like that at the end, not to mention Signora Sicilia, was pretty damned funny.
You rarely see shows this bad. A complete waste of the time I have after work. I probably should've realized what I was getting into when I saw the long list of companies in the credits.
Act III was staged successfully. Thankfully, it looks like the events of the preceding period did not interfere with the playwright's work after all. Very much looking forward to your next piece.

I just happened to stop by after work to kill some time, and I didn't expect the show to be so good. I was blown away when I saw that judge get knocked out and stuffed into the trunk. The author writes unexpected while still realistic twists, carrying a message through. Will recommend to friends.
Had to leave halfway through because something came up. But, it was still pretty touching to see three like-minded young men. You don’t see such tight-knit fratelli these days.

The title of the play caught my fancy, and I originally planned to study up on the actors, but the story itself was rather disappointing. It should've been about the history and evolution of Siracusa over the years, as well as the conflicts among the famiglie both above-board and behind-the-scenes, but they kept forcing in those strange little praises instead of treating the subject matter seriously. Also, the actors looked pretty lost.
A lot of people started walking out, so I went up to the front. There were lots of exciting fight scenes, so that was good.
My friend starred in the show, so I went to watch her. It was good. Also, goodbye.

A pretty good show, great for enjoying with friends. It's fun listening to them try to break down the plot. The introductions at the beginning were hard to keep track of; I was fine personally, but someone was about to doze off.
Like-minded youths always seem to come together. Really takes me back.
Hahaha, you sure worked your ass off, director!
I'd rather try nibbling on thistles.
A satisfying ending, exactly how the story should've ended. It’s basically the image I have in my mind.
Pretty interesting. Not much else to say.
Boring as hell.

Like so many other commenters, I was drawn in by the title. I thought it would be a historical documentary based on primary sources. I was pretty disappointed. If you're looking to study this to improve your writing, I'd stay home instead.

Quite inferior, even if we're purely speaking from the perspective of a playwright's creative process. There were actually seven main characters, all of which died in the end. Combined with the tragic music, I was left utterly speechless.
I was eating popcorn in the theater and they kicked me out. Never got to finish.

Unfortunately, I missed the beginning. It's something that happens more and more as you get older. Fortunately, the latter half was exciting. The last few stories all unfolded in the same little room, which was an interesting spin.

The playwright still needs some refinement. Beginning a story with minor characters is a common maneuver. It reflects the changing times, as well as personal development and choices. Unfortunately, the execution didn't pan out in the end.
After thinking on it, I finally decided to buy another ticket. When would be a good time to invite her to come see it? What a fascinating performance.
This eye mask is good at blocking out the light, and the performance did a great job of putting me to sleep.
If things really did end that way, that might've been better for a lot of people
Story was very interesting, but those two crooks reminded me of some former subordinates of mine who could never follow instructions. The boss's line stuck with me: 'Just don't hire idiots.'

Just the same run-of-the-mill stuff I see every day after work. You know what the playwright is trying to convey through these three characters, but unfortunately, they don’t have the skills to pull it off.

About halfway through, I decided it'd be more worthwhile to throw a party! Croissant was right, I should've sold apple pie at the door!
*Edited 3 days later* Huh? Turns out, I went to the wrong number, haha!
There are hardly any shows these days that can make me laugh out loud, and they only get fewer and farther between. So just for that alone, nine points!

This show was my Siracusan debut! A lot of unexpected things happened along the way, but the final performance turned out pretty good. It looks like the audience enjoyed it too, which makes me very happy!

A rarely-seen style. In somewhat ironic fashion, explores the true story of a multi-party struggle, reflecting the dark side of the famiglie's activities. Begins by introducing the backgrounds of a cast of characters, leading to the titular theme, then finally leaving the audience on a suspenseful note. Flows naturally, good show.

Next time, I'm going to ask the boss if we can shoot a film about a group of friends, just like this. We’ll move the setting from Lungmen to Siracusa. Dunno about anyone else, but I sure wanna star in that myself★!

Shows like this are a quick way to score fame and fortune, and the fact that it's won awards is unsurprising. However, I've been thinking recently–if people get too used to this logic, they’ll just keep talking up whoever’s actually allowed to speak, even if Grey Hall and the famiglie cease to exist.

I decided to watch it because of the reviews, so I understand where the polarized ratings come from. I remember watching a movie from Lungmen before that had some nice fights between the gangsters and the cops. What the hell was this?

An unexpectedly good ending, avoiding falling into common clichés. The youth have the power to go beyond the status quo, and see things from a broader perspective. They are the saplings of our future.

Bring your friends! I was almost kicked out for bringing pizza to the door, but we ate it on the spot. The story's really amazing, and I want to get to know the playwright. Acting in a show like this is sure to expand my acting career!

What the playwright seeks to express is evident, but unfortunately, cannot fully do so due to a lack of ability. For example, the brothers' rebellion at the end should've reflected the famiglia's principle of self-interest above all else, yet this was written off as a farce. But having that said, were it not for that bit of expressiveness, the entire opera would've been a complete waste of time.

Playwright? Bah, whoever created this doesn't deserve the title. All he knows how to do is grab some pretentious words, some inflammatory ones, and some trendy topics to bait people into paying for it. Slap this hodgepodge together, and call it a finished work!
If a Lungmen movie ever turned out this bad, a certain someone would make a fifty-long diss track.

It's clear that the playwright shifted her paradigm once, and this shift elevated the quality of the entire opera to another level, bringing it from a personal story with a heroic narrative style to an evocative Siracusan tale. That’s enough for now. I’ll save rest of my commentary for the arts papers.

The playwright's creativity is worth learning from. While everyone else uses serious narratives to tell the stories of the famiglie, this author took the completely opposite approach. Moreover, a number of coincidences occur in this show, but they are presented in a way that always feels natural and not jarring. Very impressive.

I didn't really understand what the show was getting at. I wanted to ask someone to explain it to me, but the judge lady who told me to check it out hasn’t come by. I'm not sure how she feels about it in the first place. Maybe I'm not cut out for the opera.

items.t: Never should've been put on stage
items.d: Some of my subordinates recommended me this opera. They genuinely believe in the history it recounts, as well as the lofty heights to which it lifts the famiglie. Siracusa's famiglie were never meant to be her saviors. Harboring such illusions in the first place would only serve to destroy the famiglia.

Had to walk out halfway through. On the way back, I finally figured out what was so weird. Siracusa doesn't even have police! The Lungmen-style gangster flick adapted it to a judge and the wise guys doing drive-by crossbow shootings, which was beyond hilarious. Too bad the boss isn't here, because I'd LOVE for him to get a load of this.

items.d:
A man, who has clearly consumed excessive amounts of cheap alcohol over a long period of time, is muttering ambiguously, lamenting his lack of a worthwhile life. Upon hearing that foreigners are visiting town, he finally lifts his eyelids, revealing the cloudy pupils underneath.

'Alive Until Sunset? A rock-and-roll band? Pah!' The man snorts sharply. 'Let them rock-and-roll their way back to where they belong. We all know that this is just another of the Inquisition's cheap tricks, and they're not welcome here!'

The man picks up his bottle and walks out of the tavern unsteadily. His trailing voice is still faintly audible: 'They've already ruined this place, what used to be our...'
The only things left in the tavern are wine-stained blotches and knocked-over chairs.

A ragged beggar leans against the side of the chapel, his hands clasped together tightly. He is not so much praying as simply existing, hardly any different from a pebble.

Day or night, young or old, healthy or sick, nothing matters to him. Nobody cares about him, and he also cares about nobody.

The beggar bows his head deeply, tears rolling from his eyes: 'I don't deserve to be promoted.'
The beggar bows his head deeply, tears rolling from his eyes: 'I don't deserve to be promoted.'

The devout gather around the chapel, trembling as they close their eyes. They turn around and press their foreheads against the cold wall, as if the chapel's weather-worn stone had become their last pillar of support.

'Fire! Light! He's brought light!' An old man covers his eyes, convulsing as he screeches.
The people remain as motionless as statues, the twitching old man no longer anywhere to be seen. Nobody is willing to reveal where he went.
There's nobody left in the cellar.
The arrival of outsiders has disturbed this peaceful town. It would be better to ask around at the Bitterscale Tavern.

A strange wheeled device rolls down from the pile of debris, covered in dust and missing parts but still emitting a strange glow. It's unclear what activated it, but it nevertheless whirrs to life.

Around its chassis are the words 'Little Handy' written in Ægirian. If its missing components can be found, it may prove unexpectedly helpful on the battlefield.
The only thing left here is useless garbage.
Cultists have infiltrated the town, and the growling of monsters drifts from the shadows. It is impossible to pass through here.

An old man's vigilant eyes peer out from behind the curtains. He had experienced this decades ago, and is no stranger to it. Their hopes of rebuilding are being crushed underfoot, and the instigator is someone they believed in.

The friends regarded as brothers have disappeared into the shadows, the plans into which countless hours were poured have been put on hiatus, and the imposing man with a lantern says that the cult has infiltrated you.

The old man gazes at the photo hanging upside-down over his bed. The once-dazzling sunset has faded.

And thus, a dream was shattered.

Between monsters and humans, which is truly more terrifying?
The curtains have been drawn shut, concealing the peoples' vigilant eyes.
Cultists have infiltrated the town, and their rituals are blocking the way.
A Sea Terror is curled up behind the counter, with an elderly woman sitting across from it.

A stack of diagrams lies scattered between the old woman and the Sea Terror. Though half her face is concealed by a hood, she is undoubtedly staring at the creature before her. Many years ago, she had dedicated all her talents to Iberia's greatest expedition, but that intrepidity ended in a terrifying silence.

After experiencing hardship, struggle, and disillusionment, she gave herself to a greater cause, one transcending country or geography—she sought to find the perfect other side that all living things could cross over to.

What's more, within the cult, she is able to continue the research on monsoons and hydrology that has captivated her so.

Now that the Inquisition has arrived, the products of her blood, sweat, and tears must be burned, her theories never to see the light of day. She chose to dedicate them to a Cycle of the great evolution, to a Sea Terror.

Sea Terrors roam right in front of her, but do no more than roam. Fortunately, she is patient.
There is nothing behind the counter.
There is nothing useful behind the shed.
There is nothing inside the mailbox.
Until the forward base finds a way to deal with the nethersea brand, it is inadvisable to rush ahead through this area.
Only useless debris remains in this collapsed house.
The documents in the file cabinet escape a fiery fate.
The samples in the specimen storage escape a fiery fate.

The file cabinet holds materials that the Church of the Deep's cultists have been researching for a long time. From the dates and labels, their research began many years ago.

The promise of an evolutionary end-goal is so enticing and so real that it can drive the brightest minds to work towards it day and night, sacrificing themselves.

A few lines of handwriting are scribbled onto the file's header, perhaps a spark of inspiration from the cultist who recorded it.

'What does it mean to become a part of the cycle of evolution? It means to be truly free from all suffering.'

The specimen storage contains a staggering number of samples, including photographs, anatomical diagrams, and tissue cross-sections. Some of these species have never been observed in the evolutionary record.

The promise of an evolutionary end-goal is so enticing and so real that it can drive the brightest minds to work towards it day and night, sacrificing themselves.

How did the cultists feel towards the creatures they worshipped? When their scalpels sliced through the flesh of the Sea Terror, did they feel the same pain as if their own skin was being cut?

Or will humanity's curiosity eventually supersede faith?
The documents have been removed, and the file cabinet is empty.
The samples have been removed, and the specimen storage is now empty.
Pretty much anything of value has already been whisked away, but the collectors over the years seem to have overlooked the toolbox in the corner.

Hidden inside the toolbox in the corner are several blueprints and a notepad. The blueprints, signed by chief naval architect Breogan, depict a massive battleship, the magnum opus of Iberia's Golden Age before calamity struck.

But both Gran Faro and this factory were born after the calamity, and the ships slated to be built here were nothing more than laughable toys compared to even the smallest in the fleet.

The engineers here still carry with them blueprints of things that can no longer be brought into being. Are they meant for technical reference, or are they merely holding onto a beautiful dream?

Funnily enough, even this parody of the Golden Age is filled with nothing but corpses.
There is nothing left in the factory worth investigating.
A few of the small vessels prepared beforehand by the Penal Battalion are moored in the port. When they set sail into the sea for the first time, they will face completely unknown winds and waves.

After the plan to build Gran Faro was put on hold, Coldreef Port was almost never used. The few voyages in the port's records were mostly small-scale search missions carried out by the Inquisition and the Penal Battalion.

Nobody ever returned from those expeditions.

Today, this long-since lonely port will finally see off another ship from its embrace. Its crew will set out to find the Eye of Iberia that is still looking out over the ocean.

The Penal Battalion prepared the boat in advance, the old dockworker carrying out work he was unfamiliar with: loading the vessel with supplies for the voyagers. The boat slowly left the port, disappearing from the people's sight.

The dockworker thought to himself that he might never get the chance to send off another ship in his few remaining years.
The ships have already left the port. May they return as scheduled.
There is nobody here.
There may be clues to crossing the ocean in this abandoned factory.
A long voyage is extremely dangerous. You'll need to head to Coldreef Port first to make ample preparations.

This diary records the years that the lighthouse's keepers spent here. One day, the silent waves swept through everything, and they found themselves trapped here in the middle of the ocean. At first, there was fear and panic. Then, there was an attempt to escape. Finally, they accepted their fate.

Even when dignity, civilization, and all that humans are meant to rely on are cast aside, it is not all that difficult to survive. Whenever one falls in their duties, they become nutrients for another to continue the vigil.

The text on the last page of the diary is smudged with water, now barely legible.

'All that we do, even sin and blasphemy, is not for the sake of our ultimate victory. It is for the hope that our defeat can be slightly delayed.'

Upon opening the drawers, the keepers' belongings can be seen neatly stowed inside. By the looks of it, someone had fastidiously tidied the place. There is a broken dagger in the drawer, no doubt having been in a brutal fight. There is also half a pack of tobacco, but no matches to go along with it, which must have disappointed the original owner.

There are also a few Arts Units here that have fallen apart, with signs of having been repaired as much as possible. Additionally, there is a photo, effaced by the passage of time, that is now completely unidentifiable.

A small communication terminal is located here, the knob that adjusts its frequency band worn shiny-smooth.

There are still a few pieces of weathered jerky of unclear origin.
Everything in the warehouse has already been emptied out.
There is nothing worth taking from this safe.
There is nothing left in this cabinet.

For whatever reason, the traces of the passing years can be seen on this note. It has never been moved, replaced, or dusted—always remaining in its original position, faithfully conveying the message left by the one who penned it. Day after day, year after year.

'Don't touch them. Those are my treasures, and you'll pay if anything goes missing!'

'Try to control yourself the next time you get into a fight. There aren't many things left on this ship to prove where we came from.'

After the passage of a great many moons, the original witnesses have long disappeared, but these manuscripts remain elegant and dignified.

The locked door has been opened. This area inside the lounge originally was a small conference room, but by the looks of things, the last meeting held here did not go very well. Documents are strewn all over the ground, trampled upon by panicked footprints.

A huge chart hangs in the conference room, marking the positions of every ship in the Grand Fleet. The icons that once represented their existence have all been extinguished, leaving the chart empty. Its azure background now symbolizes the boundless ocean upon which this flagship floats, alone.

And thus, the mightiest fleet ever known to Terra quietly dissolved into this blue expanse.

Join the pride and ambition of Iberia past.
There is nothing worth taking from the ship's lavatory.
Unsurprisingly, it's a Sea Terror. It stumbles to a halt and turns around.

If Sea Terrors also possess the mental state of 'confusion,' then the Sea Terror before your eyes is without a doubt confused. It seems to have been battling a wall for some time now, a side of its body thorny and chitinous from the collisions. If it has no way to leave, it will ultimately give up, turning itself into nutrients for its kin.

Its body has been impaled with a string of keys, likely remnants of its last mortal struggle. Its opponent had likely broken their blade and reached for whatever sharp objects were available, persisting until the bitter end.

Perhaps the wound just happened to cut into a certain nerve node in the Sea Terror. Or perhaps there is some other reason it escaped to the crew quarters and decided to do battle against a wall.

There might even be another possibility...

In any case, pull out the keys, and put an end to its miserable existence.
There is nothing left here except a bed that will never again offer sweet dreams to anyone.

It may well be the case that even the most skilled craftsmen of today's nations would be helpless before these devices. Not because of how complex their structure is, but rather from the difficulty of operating their Arts Units.

Most of these tools are fairly simple for a beginner to operate: a flip of a switch and a few button presses, and they'll spring to life and efficiently get the job done. The only issue is, nobody knows exactly why they work.

Just as humans cannot imagine walking without legs or grasping without hands, these machines lack any kind of reasonable engine or power supply mechanism. Only god knows how they work.

The way they use Originium is completely different.

At the bottom of the drawer is a sheet of paper that has long since yellowed. Next to it are words written in striking red paint: 'Don't go to the deck. Don't jump overboard. Don't allow yourself to sink! Read it, remember it, remember who you are!'

This piece of paper seems to have been cut from the officers' manual, and is filled with flamboyant rhetoric boasting that this ship 'can be called a palace on the Iberian Sea, a mobile throne for exalted kings.'

The officers and researchers lucky enough to be selected as the crew of the Stultifera Navis were the most outstanding talents of Iberia's Golden Age.

One of the passages was marked with a highlighter: 'In any given era, there are only so many names that will be remembered. History, in all its cruelty, shows no mercy to the mediocre. Congratulations, most glorious crewmember—you will surely enter the annals of history.'
There is nothing worth taking from the storage room.
There are still unopened rooms in the officer's lounge. Make sure there are no potential threats before continuing on.

As its name suggests, the First Galley is one of several kitchens. In addition, there's a kitchen for preparation and plating, another for desserts, and so on. The crew here is served delectable dishes worthy of their honorable statuses, or at least they were in the past.

'For example, being appointed as chief naval architect of Iberia.'

'Breogan is going to build a massive fleet for Iberia. Even a fool can see how ambitious their king is, but so be it. Perhaps Breogan spoke true—that we are but visitors on land, and our ultimate purpose is to aid Ægir.'

'All sounds have vanished. The tide is approaching.'

'A terrible wave. It will swallow us all.'

'Something must've happened to Ægir. I have to find Breogan.'

'I've already looked everywhere. Where is Breogan hiding? He couldn't have died in the Profound Silence, but the situation for him now is likely more dangerous than it was then.'

'That's right, he foresaw it long ago, but the countermeasures he prepared were taken as evidence that he was responsible for the calamity. He was branded an evil sorcerer who sacrificed Iberia to the waves. Even our identity as Ægir has become a mark of original sin, and the land-dwellers accuse us of bringing disaster in our wake.'

'I just saw an Ægir youth being beaten in a corner. The assailant was his Iberian neighbor, who he had always gotten along well with.'

'Damn it, I have to find Breogan again. No matter what happened to Ægir, we have to go back.'

Was there any point to burning himself out to do all this? He tried to find answers. Locating one's own position in the annals of history is a challenge that every person must face. He feels a little drowsy—perhaps this question wasn't as important as he originally thought. After all, things have already played out as they did.

He notices something flowing down his dry eyes, salty and bitter, reminding him of the hometown he can no longer return to. The hatred still remains in his heart, and he decides to no longer try to let it go, but instead to embrace it. That turns out to be significantly easier.

He notices something flowing down his rigid body, crimson and damp, reminding him of his ruined hometown. The responsibility still weighs on his shoulders, and he decides to no longer try to fulfill it, but instead to let it rest here. That turns out to be slightly easier.

How many heroes use fate to justify themselves, and how many fools use it to excuse themselves? He tries to brace his body with his palms once more, but fails once more. People disperse in front of him—why does this scene seem so familiar? He remembers. They had come to him the same way before.

Where could that glorious flagship be now? A pity, for only the darkened skies remain in his vision. He consoles himself that it is almost over, and as for those wishes... a human's power cannot hold out forever. Wait a bit longer. Give them a little more time.

Does that great lighthouse still stand now? A pity, for only the darkened skies remain in his vision. He consoles himself that it is almost over, and as for those dreams... a human's power cannot hold out forever. Wait a bit longer. Give them a little more time.

Very well, the end has come. He suddenly realizes that he seems willing to accept this outcome. Of course, as his final resting place, this place is too cold and too hard, a far cry from the comfort of a pillow, from resting his eyes by a warm fire. Not to mention, his gut has been punctured several times, and his lifeblood oozes out.

But, it could be worse. He decides to forgive those who are quickly dispersing, slinking back into the shadows. If their positions were reversed, he might feel the same anger.

He gave it his all, and failed. He could not beat the ocean at its game after all. But maybe he didn't lose too badly. Those who put him to death are still willing to feel anger, and is that not hope?

'Good luck, my friends. To those above land, and to those beneath the sea.'

'What the hell was that? Why is this happening to Gran Faro? First the Ægir, then the cultists, and now these damned monsters! I need to leave this place! Otherwise... Otherwise...!'

'I've seen it with my own eyes! The Inquisition's flames will burn a person's soul dry!'

'I leave these things to you!'

Sheds still line the shores, offering a glimpse of how bustling this small town used to be. People from all over used to arrive, trying to restore a glimmer of hope following the calamity. But now, it's been abandoned, its sheets of metal rusting away. The precious materials once used to build this place are now scattered about everywhere, no longer of anyone's concern.

This place may have been inhabited by Ægir Islanders, as the signboards bear faintly-visible patterns distinct from the Iberian style. Now, it is completely uninhabited. And when the previous inhabitants left, they lacked the time to even take their supplies with them.

This is the lighthouse the elders spoke of, the 'Eye of Iberia' in Jordi's dreams. These corridors, stairs, and panels may once have been tread upon and touched by his parents.

Jordi tries to feel an aura of familiarity from them. Countless times, he has sketched his parents' likenesses from his imagination, the way they would shuttle between lighthouses. Those few notes left behind correspond to reality, line by line.

Perhaps their bones are still interred somewhere in this lighthouse. The thought makes Jordi shudder. Now he stands at the same place, his hand covering the same control panel. Where, then, will fate take him?

Jordi decides not to think about these things. He must accomplish his duties, irrespective of his identity, his worth, or his beliefs.

Jordi stands here for the sake of his unrealistic dreams, and though he may be anxious and uncertain, the one thing he is not, is lost.
The warehouse holds supplies designated for the next voyage. The only problem? Nobody knows when that will be, or if it will ever happen.

In a half-opened safe sits an outdated nautical chart, once used by the old Iberian fleet to conquer the seas. The crystallization of their explorations through the mist. Unfortunately, it is now nothing more than scrap paper. A few other miscellaneous items also sit at the bottom of the safe, with nobody left to use them.

Inside the bathroom, everything looks good as new, and drops of water dribble from the spigot. The only unusual thing is that all the mirrors have been shattered, now only able to reflect broken images. There are still unused supplies in the storage box under the sink.

A storage room full of spare sails. Unfold one, and you will find a canvas decorated with golden threads, and carefully embroidered with the pattern of the Iberian flag. Maybe there are some useful supplies to be found here.

The anchor system was completely destroyed during the Profound Silence, and this cabin has been empty for many years. However, someone seems to have turned this place into their own secret stash, leaving behind quite a few glittering things.

The drafting room was once used to aggregate the results of exploration and draft nautical charts. After the calamity, the entire ocean's currents, prevailing winds, and uncharted islands all underwent tremendous changes, rendering the laws formulated over generations completely meaningless. Some usable supplies can still be found here.

Nobody knows what these discarded barrels were once used for. Perhaps over six decades ago, they were filled with spirits that the crew would drink in celebration. Now only a few tattered relics sit at the bottom of the barrel. Who was the desperate seaman who exchanged these things for the last sip of wine?

The Penal Battalion shows no weakness. The Penal Battalion shall not yield. The Penal Battalion is Iberia's bastion, and even the terrible waves do nothing more than wash away any impurities. From this supply station, the soldiers stare at the Iberian soil now swallowed by the ocean.
'These days, I will occasionally dream. Of dazzling golden domes, of my humid hometown.'
'I have never felt water in this form before—soft, cold, beautiful, and deadly.'
'These flames blaze more passionately than any I have felt before, perhaps because my partner in this conversation is that extraordinary.'
'Breogan brought with him not only dreams of gold, but also a warning from the sea. Most people chose to ignore the latter.'
'Nobody can resist their own desires, especially when you understand when they are desiring.'
'Where there is light, there is also a shadow. The brighter the light, the deeper the darkness.'
'As a friend, Alfonso is absolutely qualified. As a captain... Fine, there isn't anyone to compare him to anyway.'
This piece of paper has been waterlogged for so long that the letters on it are no longer legible.
'Soil is the cradle of life. They say that when the spring wind blows, green shoots will sprout here.'
'I can feel the excitement in each and every one of us. We are about to face a cornerstone of the truth.'
'Those with power tend to underestimate their ability. Even more so for those with great power.'
'Once ambition germinates, it knows only how to proliferate. Even if it's clear it will only lead to ruin.'
'Do you hear the sound of the tides? It's as if someone is sobbing.'
'Friends, we are all starting to get old. Yesterday, Breogan spent half the day complaining about his new wrinkles. I think it's because he frowns too much.'
'...Leviathan...Ægir...lost...Abyssal Hunters... This plan is our last hope.'

A rumor began to circulate in the shelter from the encroaching waters: Breogan, the man who invited the Silence, died in an alley as punishment for angering the sea. This news did not particularly make any waves, as the people were more concerned with whether they'd go hungry tomorrow.

A warped mailbox with a strange device crammed into it, the words 'Wilderness Survival Module' printed on the side in Ægirian, seemingly slotting into 'Little Handy.' Who put it here, and what message are they trying to send to whom?

Open the cabinet's swaying doors, and a complex-looking device can be found resting inside. A thin line of Ægirian text along its side reads: 'Housekeeping Assistant Module.' It seems to fit into one of the slots on 'Little Handy.' It appears to have been carefully stashed here at some point, but where did it come from?

In the maintenance access corridor, a special device can be found leaning against the wall, marked with the Ægirian letters, 'Incremental Motion Firmware.' It seems to fit into one of the slots on 'Little Handy.' Hard to imagine how this thing can be used to help people exercise.

The Stultifera Navis is not only a battleship, but also houses a large number of research facilities. The unrecognizable equipment in the hydrology workstation regularly makes noises, but there is no longer anyone who can interpret them.

A delicate device has been placed here, its underside labeled with a single line of Ægirian: 'Mini Decontamination Kit.' It seems to fit into one of the slots on 'Little Handy.'

'When did Breogan bring his Little Handy with him onto land? If I knew earlier, I would've brought mine too—it always helps me get the colors I need. He even bought an External Upgrade Module for it! That thing's expensive as hell!'

This road has already become scantly traveled. Nobody cares about the stories that once unfolded here, nobody remains to record them. Silence falls upon all equally, bringing the same quietude. Only the street sign marks these memories, roughly engraved with the name of this small town— 'Gran Faro.'

Nobody knows why this lighthouse survived the disaster, but perhaps it is because no matter how terrifying the wind and waves may be, nothing can stop people from gazing towards the sea. Iberia's eyes will never close, only be temporarily clouded over.

When disaster struck, both the great flagship Stultifera Navis—the Ship of Fools—and the Iberian fleet to which it belonged were out at sea. Giant waves swallowed everything, but the ghosts of the past still lingered.

The huge dome elevator in the middle of the Stultifera connects the various levels of this great battleship. When riding it, one may witness Iberia's breathtaking scenery depicted across the walls. Standing here is like standing in the center of the world.
On the main deck, the nethersea brand is spreading. It mercilessly engulfs everything, irreversibly. This is how it survives, able to heal wounds left even by the passage of time.
This part of the ocean may have had a name once, but that no longer matters. The premise for a name to be born is that something needs to be distinguished. But now, the ocean is the ocean.

items.t: The 4 cities of Kawalerielki have successfully docked together, raising the curtain on the Kazimierz Major

blocks.p: Last night, the Knights Association announced the twelve division spokespeople for this season. They will represent the sponsors, the Knights Association and the National Council to ensure that the Major proceeds without incident. During the appointment ceremony, the twelve spokespeople performed their first duty in collectively announcing the passing of a bill by the National Council back in May: All convicted knights with outstanding contributions shall be granted a commuted sentence.

To allow each and every knight to achieve glory and hone their skills has long been the unchanging motto of the Kazimierz Major. We look forward to seeing the valiant knights during the preliminaries for each division.

items.t: The Radiant Knight appears once more? Will the debuting knight of the Nearl family restore honor to the nobility?

blocks.p: The preliminaries of the Kazimierz Major have been ongoing for several months now. Besides the seven Knightclubs directly invited to join the Major and the four Knight Orders, the remaining knights have been competing against one another to accumulate points in the preliminaries.
However, an unexpected contestant appeared yesterday in the West Division's Roar Arena——Maria Nearl. This is a big deal for any knightwatcher.

Six years ago, the Radiant Knight who shot to fame after winning the championship was expelled when it was discovered she had concealed her infection, causing the old and once prestigious family to fall into the awkward situation of not having a presiding Knight Primus. Back then, Młynar Nearl who was pushed to the forefront refused the Knights Association's invitation, and the Nearl family was on the brink of losing their noble status.

In the end, the National Council declared that should the Nearl family not present a new Knight Primus with a legitimate title within five years, they would be stripped of their nobility. Maria Nearl's performance in the current season will determine the fate of the Nearl family.
We will watch this young knight closely.
Specially chosen for you by Big Data

items.t: More than a hundred knights join the banquet held by the Northwood Order!

blocks.p: The name 'Northwood' should not be unfamiliar to any knight who follows the Kazimierz Major. As one of the Knight Orders of Kazimierz and still in its prime, there are many veteran Knightclubs under its banner such as the Blade Helmet Knightclub and the Spikeshield Knightclub. With no other Knightclubs promoted to Knight Orders this year, Northwood has managed to maintain their hold on the Central Division, but the situation remains dismal as the Knight Orders of the other Divisions continue to eye them eagerly.

The stated objective of the banquet is to celebrate the several new knight contestants, but it is easy to ascertain that more than half the invited knights are unaffiliated and even untitled independent knights. Obviously, to continue remaining an 'Order' and avoid falling to the status of a 'Club', Northwood has decided to expand during the current season to avoid a poor showing. We watch with bated breath to see how many are attracted by the promised cake.
Specially chosen for you by Big Data

items.t: Qualitative Report on the Suborning of Infected: Kindness does not imply indulgence

blocks.p: This year is the third since the inception of the Infected Participation System. We are extremely happy to announce that this humanitarian initiative has achieved significant results, with Infected-related incidents dropping substantially in many areas. The comportment of the Infected fighting for their lives has won them unique respect as well as tangible wealth they require for survival.

However, as the number of Infected participants increases year-on-year, problems have inevitably cropped up. Besides the challenge of getting proper treatment to Infected knights, some Infected who have attained great wealth through competitions and their fighting skills have begun to buy over their Infected kin and set up private organizations unrecognized by the Knights Association. These organizations are heavily suspected to be involved in illegal fundraising and holding armed rallies with the goal of disrupting social stability and taking revenge against non-Infected.

Currently, the Knights Association has filed a legal complaint to the National Council requesting to remedy the problem of Infected knights taking in large numbers of illegal Infected. Kazimierz will never allow the 'Great Kawalerielki Separation' incident to happen ever again.

items.t: '10 Years in the making' Mid-Tournament Special Report

blocks.p: After approval by the Knights Association and a unanimous vote from the National Council, the Tyrell Knightclub which has long been sponsored by the Ellen Select Technology Co. and a fierce contender within the Top 100 Knightclubs has finally been promoted to a Knight Order. Currently, there are only two Knightclubs under the banner of the Tyrell Knight Order: The Rachel Knightclub composed of the original members and renamed after the leader's surname, and the Warwhip Knightclub responsible for training young reserve knights. Though they are lacking in numbers, the addition of the former second runner-up Frost Skull Knight as an instructor in the Warwhip Knightclub has made waves.

At the same time, with the approval of the Knights Association, the first superstar of the current season has emerged even before the preliminaries have ended, receiving a knight's title after yesterday evening's match. With her outstanding ability, incredibly high number of votes and rapidly rising point ranking, independent knight Justyna managed to attract the attention of many companies, earning her the title of 'Fartooth' early this morning.

No matter if it's 'Fartooth' Justyna or Tyrell Knight Order, all of this signifies the outstanding development of the Kazimierz competition industry. We look forward to seeing what new trends will come from this season of the Kazimierz Major.

items.t: Nearl's Secret Base? Secret Bar Exposed! You Won't Believe Which Knights Drink Here!

blocks.p: At the end of Golden Feather Street, there is an unassuming bar with a strange name——Scary Martin. Such bars can be found all over Kazimierz, but this one is unique for one particular reason most people are unaware of. This bar's regular clientele are almost all retired knights.

That isn't what's important, though. The real story is the Radiant Knight's sister Maria Nearl and the Whislash Knight Zofia, who are often in the area after the bar closes. Most bars don't close so early, and it's a bit of a stretch to say that it's because of bad business. But Maria and Whislash have been frequently seen near the bar. I'm sure everyone is familiar with Maria, and as an independent knight her relationship with Whislash was once a hot topic. Even after Maria joined the Major representing the Nearl family, Młynar Nearl, who was once pushed for the same position kept quiet. According to his coworkers, he has paid no attention to it and is still working an ordinary job, as if he has nothing to do with it.

Perhaps the secret behind the Nearl family lies within this bar. Your correspondent has no other information to report for now, but readers who wish to witness the Nearls' grace may want to try their luck.
